summary: Iteration 5 — verification of the intermittent-404 bug fixes. RESULT: both reported 404 sources are FIXED. (1) HEAD /api/media/{id} now returns 200 with a body-less response and byte-identical ETag / Accept-Ranges / Cache-Control / Content-Length headers vs GET (verified header-by-header on a real image + real video file taken from Mongo db.files where is_deleted=false); 5 consecutive HEADs all 200 (no intermittency); HEAD on a bogus id returns 404 (no longer 405). (2) POST /api/auth/refresh: 401 without a token, 401 with a garbage Bearer, 200 with a valid Bearer returning a fresh JWT + public user payload, and the new token is accepted by GET /api/auth/me. (3) Regression sweep: all 12 requested authenticated endpoints return 200 for Deniz (/auth/me, /feed, /portfolio, /portfolio/transactions, /portfolio/performance, /notifications, /market/movers, /market/search?q=THYAO, /users/deniz.yatirim, /users/deniz.yatirim/posts, /users/deniz.yatirim/disclosures, /alerts) with no _id leakage. (4) Symbol search: all 15 variants (THYAO, THYAO.IS, BIST:THYAO, thyao, türk hava, TUPRS, tüpraş, aselsan, bim, koç holding, ASTOR, asto, GARAN, EREGL, MGROS) return the correct top hit. (5) Frontend: a post whose image_url points at a nonexistent media id DOES render (text, like/comment footer) and the container is display:none — no broken-image icon; a legitimate video post renders a visible, playable

minor.issue: Route does not exist -> 405 Method Not Allowed. Users (and the testing harness) cannot delete their own posts; test/temporary posts can only be purged directly from Mongo. Add an owner-scoped DELETE that also cascades likes/comments/notifications and marks the referenced db.files record is_deleted=true (which would also fix the orphan-file growth reported in iteration 4: db.files is now 72 docs).

image_url / video_url are not validated. Posting image_url='/api/media/' (empty id) or '/api/media/<nonexistent-uuid>' is accepted with 200, which is exactly what produces the browser-side 404 loops the user complained about. Validate that a local /api/media/{id} URL resolves to an existing non-deleted db.files record (404/422 otherwise).

Observed one transient 502: Emergent Object Storage returned 500 for a 1.1 MB video/mp4 PUT (backend.err.log 'Upload failed ... 500 Server Error ... /objstore/api/v1/storage/objects/...'); an immediate retry of the identical file succeeded. A size sweep (8 KB / 200 KB / 900 KB / 1.5 MB images, 200 KB / 1.1 MB videos) is 6/6 green, so this is storage flakiness, not a size limit. put_object has no retry/backoff (get_object does) — add one, otherwise users see intermittent 'Yükleme başarısız'.

The app sets Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400 but the response observed through the public URL is 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' (rewritten upstream), so media is never browser-cached: the broken-image post triggered 5 separate GET .../api/media/... 404s in one page session. Not a code bug, but it amplifies any bad URL into a 404 storm — worth noting for the user's 'intermittent 404' perception.

The doc still claims 'JWT access token (15 min) + refresh token (7 days)'. Reality: single access token, ACCESS_TTL_MIN = 7 days, and /auth/refresh only rotates that same access token and REQUIRES an already-valid token — so it cannot recover an expired session. Either implement a real refresh token or correct the doc.

ui_bugs.issue: The onError handler hides the whole media container with NO fallback (no placeholder, no 'medya yüklenemedi' note). Verified side-effect: in a browser without H.264 (headless Chromium), a perfectly valid mp4 served with 206 fires MediaError code 4 and the post silently renders as text-only. A WebM in the same feed plays fine, so this is a codec/fallback UX gap, not a backend bug — but real users on codec-limited browsers will see a video post with no indication a video existed. Suggest a lightweight placeholder instead of display:none.

Navigating to /notifications silently lands on /feed (no notifications route; only the header bell panel exists). Either add the route or remove/redirect explicitly — a deep link/bookmark to notifications appears as a 'lost' page to the user.

rca_of_the_issue: The user's intermittent 404s had three sources, all now understood: (1) HEAD /api/media/{id} was unrouted -> Starlette answered 405, and browsers/video preloaders issue HEAD before a ranged GET, so media probes failed sporadically depending on which path the browser took; a HEAD handler now exists and matches GET's headers. (2) POST /api/auth/refresh was documented but unimplemented -> hard 404 whenever anything called it; implemented as a token rotation guarded by get_current_user (401 without a valid token). (3) The dominant remaining source was DATA, not code: posts created by earlier test runs carried image_url/video_url pointing at media ids that no longer exist in db.files. I enumerated all 36 distinct media ids that ever 404'd in backend.out.log — none of them is referenced by any post in the current DB, and a full scan found 0 broken media references today, so the historical storm came from now-deleted test posts. Because POST /api/posts does not validate media URLs and media responses are not browser-cacheable, one such bad post produced 5 repeated 404s per page view — hence 'ara ara' (intermittent). Adding URL validation on post creation (and a real DELETE that cleans up files) closes the loop.
